name: Suki
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_citation: van Tongeren, Charlotte. 2022. A grammar of Suki, a language of Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl:1885/278358 (file, ANU Open Research Repository).
catalog_quote: Stress on words spoken in isolation is on the initial syllable, e.g. ˈatu ‘woman’, ˈrauka-rete [paddle-fut]. A number of tamp inflections on the verb influence stress placement; this is indicated in the discussions in Chapter 8. A number of tamp-particle units influence stress placement on the predicate of the clause; this is indicated in the discussions in Chapter 12. ... [§7.1] The subject and predicate constituents are additionally differentiated through their respective stress patterns. Regular stress in Suki is word-initial, but stress on clause-final constituents is shifted to penultimate when they host the cliticising tpu (§10.2). [fn.1: i.e. penultimate when the tpu itself is counted as the ultimate syllable.] ... [fn.2:] The only constituents for which stress is not shifted under the conditions described are nps with indefinite marker itu. ... [§8.4.1, future imperative] the in…

audit.reasoning: Quote check: all deciding passages confirmed verbatim in the ANU thesis PDF we hold at the cited pages (pp.73, 192, 245). Deciding source is a 2022 586-page reference grammar (PhD, ANU), the first and only comprehensive description of Suki per the author and per Glottolog (3 descriptive refs total; the other two are an unpublished 50-pp sketch and the same author's 2013 workshop talk). The classification (fixed word-initial, weight-blind, no secondary stress described; clitic/TAM-conditioned shifts recorded as perturbations) matches the grammar's explicit statements 'Stress on words spoken in isolation is on the initial syllable' and 'Regular stress in Suki is word-initial'. Voorhoeve 1970 (PL C-13), downloaded now from the open Pacific Linguistics archive, independently reports primary stress 'in most of the cases on the first vowel' (p.1263), confirming. No instrumental study exists to my knowle

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1970. Some notes on the Suki-Gogodala subgroup of the Central and South New Guinea Phylum. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds.), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell (Pacific Linguistics C-13), 1245-1270. Canberra: ANU.
sources.quote: 'In the words I recorded, a primary stress falls in most of the cases on the first vowel, diphthong, or triphthong. I could not ascertain whether stress is phonemic or not.' Also: 'In many instances I noted extra vowel length. In all these cases the vowel appeared to be stressed ... I will regard length as non-distinctive.'
sources.locator: Appendix A (Suki phonology), 'Accent', p.1263 (p.18); also p.1262-1263 on length under stress
sources.note: Only independent (pre-2022) first-hand phonological note on Suki; its Appendix A 'Accent' reports primary stress mostly on the first vowel, an independent confirmation of the word-initial coding. downloaded now.
